# s3b CLI reference

<!-- Generated by "go run ./tools/gendocs" from the cobra command tree. -->
<!-- Do not edit by hand: regenerate with the command above instead.       -->

`s3b` is the command-line face of S3 Bucket Browser. Run it without
arguments to launch the desktop GUI; run it with any argument to use the CLI
described here. The same engine backs both.

- **Global flags** — every command accepts the persistent flags documented on
  [`s3b`](#s3b) itself (`--profile`, `--json`, `--verbose`, `--timeout`,
  credential/addressing overrides).
- **S3 URIs** — commands address storage as `s3://bucket/prefix/`; a trailing
  slash marks a folder/prefix.
- **Environment** — `S3B_CONFIG` (config directory), `S3B_PROFILE` (default
  profile), `S3B_ACCESS_KEY` / `S3B_SECRET_KEY` (credential fallback),
  `S3B_NO_KEYRING=1` (keep secrets in the config file instead of the OS
  keyring).
- **Exit codes** — `0` success, `1` operation failure, `2` usage/config
  error, `3` unexpected error.
- **Safety ladder** — destructive operations count first and act second:
  prefix deletes over 50 objects require `--force`, non-empty bucket removal
  requires `--force`, permanent version destruction is L3.

## s3b

S3 Bucket Browser — manage S3 buckets and objects (GUI + CLI in one)

### Synopsis

s3b is the CLI face of S3 Bucket Browser.
Run without arguments to launch the desktop GUI (milestone M2).
Documentation: https://github.com/MikkoP88/s3-bucket-browser

### Options

```
      --access-key string      access key override ($S3B_ACCESS_KEY)
      --endpoint-url string    override the profile endpoint URL
      --json                   machine-readable JSON output
      --no-color               disable colors (also honors $NO_COLOR)
      --path-style             force path-style addressing
      --profile string         profile name (default: $S3B_PROFILE, then the default profile)
      --region string          override the region
      --secret-key string      secret key override ($S3B_SECRET_KEY)
      --session-token string   session token override
      --timeout duration       per-request timeout (default 5m0s)
      --verbose                verbose output
      --virtual-hosted         force virtual-hosted addressing

```

## s3b bucket lock

Show (or enable) the object-lock configuration

### Synopsis

Without flags prints the object-lock configuration.
Object lock can only be ENABLED at bucket creation (`s3b mb --object-lock`) — AWS/MinIO
refuse enabling it on existing buckets; it is permanent and cannot be disabled later.
--enable with --mode/--days sets/updates the default retention rule of a lock-enabled bucket.

```
s3b bucket lock s3://bucket [--enable] [--mode GOVERNANCE|COMPLIANCE] [--days N] [flags]
```

### Options

```
      --days int32    default retention days
      --enable        enable object lock (irreversible)
      --mode string   default retention mode (GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE)

```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --access-key string      access key override ($S3B_ACCESS_KEY)
      --endpoint-url string    override the profile endpoint URL
      --json                   machine-readable JSON output
      --no-color               disable colors (also honors $NO_COLOR)
```

## s3b completion bash

Generate the autocompletion script for bash

### Synopsis

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(s3b completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	s3b completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/s3b

#### macOS:

	s3b completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/s3b

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.


```
s3b completion bash
```

### Options

```
      --no-descriptions   disable completion descriptions
```

## s3b cp

Copy files (local↔S3, S3→S3 server-side)

### Synopsis

Directions: local→s3:// (upload), s3://→local (download), s3://→s3:// (server-side copy),
plus NAME:// source URIs (any saved non-S3 source) on either side.
SRC or DST being a directory/prefix (or --recursive) copies everything beneath it.

```
s3b cp SRC DST [flags]
```

### Options

```
      --dry-run                show what would transfer, do nothing
      --no-clobber             skip uploads when the object already exists
  -r, --recursive              copy everything under a prefix/directory
      --sse string             server-side encryption (AES256)
      --storage-class string   storage class (STANDARD, GLACIER, ...)
```

## s3b find

Deep search objects by name, size, age or storage class

### Synopsis

Streams every object under the prefix and prints the ones matching all filters.
--name is a substring, or a glob when it contains * or ? (matched against the full key,
so 'backup*' also matches nested paths). Sizes accept 10MB / 1.5GB forms; ages 30d / 24h.

```
s3b find s3://bucket[/prefix] [flags]
```

### Options

```
      --class string     exact storage class (e.g. GLACIER)
      --larger string    match objects larger than this (e.g. 10MB)
      --limit int        stop after N matches (0 = unlimited)
  -n, --name string      substring or glob to match against the key
      --newer string     last modified within this (e.g. 24h)
      --older string     last modified longer ago than this (e.g. 30d)
      --smaller string   match objects smaller than this (e.g. 500KB)

```
